reviews.question: In a four-player standard game, how many Escape Pods are selected, how are they distributed and oriented, and which tokens start in the Intruder bag?
reviews.observed_answer:
1. For four players select 3 random-numbered Pods: lowest number in Section A, next in B, then alternate A/B; all start Locked side up.
2. Put 1 Blank, 4 Larvae, 1 Creeper, 1 Queen, 3 Adults plus 1 additional Adult per player (7 Adults at four players) in the bag.
reviews.observed_evidence: “For four players select 3 random-numbered Pods: lowest number in Section A, next in B, then alternate A/B; all start Locked side up.” (Setup)
reviews.expected_answer: Three random pods; lowest numbered in A, next B, next A, all Locked. Bag: 1 Blank, 4 Larvae, 1 Creeper, 1 Queen, 7 Adults.
reviews.reason: Gives three randomly selected Locked Pods in A/B/A and the complete starting bag including seven Adults.

reviews.question: How are Objectives filtered and dealt, when does each player choose one, what happens to the rejected card, and do Eggs trigger that choice?
reviews.observed_answer:
1. Remove Corporate and Personal Objective cards showing a player count above the actual count; shuffle decks separately and deal each player one of each, hidden, before Character draft.
2. At the First Encounter, each player chooses one of their two Objectives and removes the other face down from game; nobody may inspect others’ removed cards.
3. Eggs are not Intruders and do not trigger First Encounter/Objective choice.
reviews.observed_evidence: “Remove Corporate and Personal Objective cards showing a player count above the actual count; shuffle decks separately and deal each player one of each, hidden, before Character draft.” (Setup; First Encounter)
reviews.expected_answer: Remove Objectives requiring more players than present; deal one Personal and one Corporate secretly. First Intruder miniature of any type appearing triggers immediate choice by everyone before resolving its Encounter. Remove rejected card face down unseen. Eggs do not trigger it.
reviews.reason: Explicit filtering, hidden separate deal, each player's choice at the named First Encounter, unseen rejected-card removal and Egg exclusion. First Encounter is an acceptable named trigger; an additional definition is not demanded.

reviews.question: You use an Action card with printed cost 2 while holding that card, two other Action cards and two Contamination cards. What is discarded, and can Contamination substitute for payment? What if the card offers OR effects?

requested_parts.part: Played card plus exactly two additional Action cards
Total number of Action cards discarded
requested_parts.reason: The same answer says all four Action cards leave although only three Action cards were held and the stated payment totals three.

reviews.observed_answer:
1. Discard the used Action card plus exactly two other Action cards for its printed cost 2; with two other Action cards the payment is possible and all four Action cards leave the hand.
2. Contamination cards cannot pay any Action cost.
3. Choose one of the card’s OR sections.
reviews.observed_evidence: “Discard the used Action card plus exactly two other Action cards for its printed cost 2; with two other Action cards the payment is possible and all four Action cards leave the hand.” (Actions)
reviews.expected_answer: Discard the played card and two additional Action cards face up. Contamination cannot pay costs. Choose one OR effect.
reviews.reason: The played card plus exactly two other Action cards is correct, but the same sentence falsely concludes that all four Action cards leave the hand. The stated hand contains only three Action cards; Contamination cannot supply a fourth. This internal material payment contradiction makes the answer incorrect despite its other correct clauses.

reviews.question: A Character in a burning Room takes one Action then passes. When do they take Fire damage, can they act again this Player Phase, can they discard cards, and do later players rounds burn them again?
reviews.observed_answer:
1. After finishing their own round, including the round in which they take one Action and pass, they suffer one Light Wound for ending in Fire.
2. After passing they cannot take further normal Actions that Player Phase, but may discard any number of hand cards when passing; FAQ permits Interruption after passing.
3. Later players’ rounds do not cause this Character another Fire wound; only their own round-end check applies.
reviews.observed_evidence: “After finishing their own round, including the round in which they take one Action and pass, they suffer one Light Wound for ending in Fire.” (Turn Structure; Fire markers)
reviews.expected_answer: At end of own round take 1 Light Wound. Passing bars normal Actions this Player Phase, but official FAQ permits Interruption after passing. May discard any number of hand cards on passing. No further Fire wounds from later players rounds this turn.
reviews.reason: Correct own-round-end Light Wound, no further normal Actions with explicit Interruption exception, optional passing discard and no damage from later players' rounds.

reviews.question: Describe entering an empty unexplored Room: tile, Item Counter, Exploration effect, Noise roll and token destination. How do Silence, Danger and an already occupied destination alter the Noise roll?
reviews.observed_answer:
1. Enter the neighboring Room; if tile face down, flip it, set Item count by aligning token number with board Item Counter (except Nest/Slime Room), resolve its symbol, then remove token to box.
2. If destination is empty, make Noise roll unless Exploration Silence/Danger replaces it; Silence means no roll, Danger moves all eligible non-Combat neighboring Intruders in, or if none places Noise in each connected unmarked Corridor.
3. If any Character or Intruder is already in destination, do not make the ordinary Noise roll.
4. Slime marks Character, Fire/Malfunction marks Room, Doors places token in entry Corridor.
reviews.observed_evidence: “Enter the neighboring Room; if tile face down, flip it, set Item count by aligning token number with board Item Counter (except Nest/Slime Room), resolve its symbol, then remove token to box.” (Movement; Exploration tokens; Noise roll)
reviews.expected_answer: Reveal Room and Exploration token; set counter to token number except Nest/Slime Room; resolve effect and remove Exploration token from game. Roll Noise in empty Room unless Silence or Danger exploration cancels it. Occupied Room (Character or Intruder) gives no movement Noise roll.
reviews.reason: Correct reveal/counter exclusions, effect/removal, empty-destination roll with explicit Silence/Danger cancellation and occupied-destination exception; no omitted movement Noise exception.

reviews.question: What does Careful Movement cost and replace, when is it forbidden, and can a Closed Door be crossed or a miniature stop in a Corridor?
reviews.observed_answer:
1. Careful Movement costs 2 Action cards and replaces the post-move Noise roll with a Noise marker in a chosen connected Corridor; FAQ says it also replaces automatic Silence/Danger Exploration results.
2. Cannot use in Combat or if every Corridor connected to destination already has Noise; normal Movement restrictions still apply.
3. Closed Doors block player passage; miniatures may never stop in Corridors.
reviews.observed_evidence: “Careful Movement costs 2 Action cards and replaces the post-move Noise roll with a Noise marker in a chosen connected Corridor; FAQ says it also replaces automatic Silence/Danger Exploration results.” (Basic Actions; Movement)
reviews.expected_answer: Cost 2 Action cards; replaces post-movement Noise roll with placing Noise in a chosen connected Corridor. Forbidden in Combat or when all destination Corridors have Noise. Closed Doors block player movement; no miniature stops in Corridors.
reviews.reason: Correct cost two, chosen connected Noise replacement, Combat/all-corridors-full bans, Closed Door blocking and no miniature stopping in a Corridor.

reviews.question: You roll a number for a Corridor already holding Noise, with a Technical Corridors Entrance in your Room. Give the Encounter sequence, Noise removal, token destination and Surprise Attack comparison; do Contamination cards count?
reviews.observed_answer:
1. If instructed to place Noise in an already marked Corridor, resolve an Encounter instead; first discard all Noise from Room-connected Corridors, including shared Technical Corridor if applicable.
2. Draw token, place matching miniature; compare its number with triggering player’s hand counting Action and Contamination cards; fewer cards means Surprise Attack against that player. Set non-Blank drawn token aside outside bag.
3. A Technical Corridors Noise marker occupies the shared space and counts for every Technical Entrance; the usual one-marker limit applies.
reviews.observed_evidence: “If instructed to place Noise in an already marked Corridor, resolve an Encounter instead; first discard all Noise from Room-connected Corridors, including shared Technical Corridor if applicable.” (Noise roll; Technical Corridors; Encounters)
reviews.expected_answer: Resolve Encounter: remove all connected Noise including Technical Corridors; draw bag token; place matching Intruder; compare token number to all cards in triggering hand including Contamination. Fewer cards causes Surprise Attack against triggerer, equal or more does not. Set token aside.
reviews.reason: Correct duplicate-Noise Encounter sequence, all connected Noise including Technical, token set aside and fewer-hand-cards Surprise against triggerer counting Contamination.

reviews.question: How does Danger resolve with several eligible neighboring Intruders, and when none are eligible? Does moving an Intruder into your Room count as an Encounter? How does Slime affect Silence?
reviews.observed_answer:
1. Danger moves all Intruders in neighboring Rooms that are not in Combat with any Character into the entered Room.
2. If none, or all neighboring Intruders are in Combat, place Noise in every connected Corridor lacking a marker, including Technical Corridors if there is an Entrance.
3. Mere movement of Intruder into Character Room is not an Encounter.
4. Slime makes Silence resolve as Danger.
reviews.observed_evidence: “Danger moves all Intruders in neighboring Rooms that are not in Combat with any Character into the entered Room.” (Exploration tokens; Noise roll; Encounters)
reviews.expected_answer: Move all neighboring Intruders not in Combat into current Room. If none eligible, put Noise in each connected Corridor lacking it including Technical Corridors. Moving Intruder into occupied Room is Combat, not Encounter. Slime converts Silence Noise/exploration results to Danger.
reviews.reason: Moves all eligible neighboring Intruders, otherwise fills connected unmarked Corridors including Technical, distinguishes mere movement from Encounter and converts Silence under Slime.

reviews.question: During an Encounter you draw Blank. What happens to Noise and the Blank; when is an Adult added? Contrast Blank in bag development.
reviews.observed_answer:
1. Place Noise in every Corridor connected to Room; no miniature appears; return Blank to bag.
2. If Blank was last token in bag, add one Adult token if available, otherwise none, then return Blank.
3. Add one Adult token if any available, then return Blank; this branch does not specify Noise placement.
reviews.observed_evidence: “Place Noise in every Corridor connected to Room; no miniature appears; return Blank to bag.” (Encounters; Intruder bag development)
reviews.expected_answer: Encounter replaces connected Noise in every Corridor; return Blank; add Adult only if Blank was last token in bag and a spare Adult is available; no miniature or Surprise Attack. Development always attempts adding one available Adult then returns Blank.
reviews.reason: Correct Blank Noise restoration/return, last-token and spare-token restriction for Encounter Adult addition and available-Adult development addition.

reviews.question: Two Intruders attempt to move together from the same Room through one Closed Door. Where do they end, what happens to the Door, can it later close, and would a Noise-triggered appearance be blocked by that Door?
reviews.observed_answer:
1. Both stay in their starting Room; the Closed Door is destroyed (lay token down).
2. Destroyed Door permits movement and cannot be closed again (except Plasma Torch).
3. An Intruder appearing through a Closed Door because of Noise is not blocked; it appears regardless.
reviews.observed_evidence: “Both stay in their starting Room; the Closed Door is destroyed (lay token down).” (Doors)
reviews.expected_answer: Both stay in original Room and destroy Door simultaneously. Destroyed Door permits movement but cannot close except Plasma Torch. Noise-triggered appearance ignores Closed Door.
reviews.reason: Both Intruders stay and destroy Door; destroyed movement/closure state and Noise appearance ignoring Closed Door match.

reviews.question: An injured Intruder moves into Technical Corridors with Noise already there. What happens to its miniature, injuries, token and Noise? Can Characters or Doors normally use those Corridors?
reviews.observed_answer:
1. Remove miniature, discard all its Injury markers, return its token to bag; existing Noise marker on shared Technical space remains.
2. Characters normally cannot use Technical Corridors, except Mechanic Technical Corridors Action or Technical Corridor Plans Item.
3. Door tokens can never be placed in Technical Corridors.
reviews.observed_evidence: “Remove miniature, discard all its Injury markers, return its token to bag; existing Noise marker on shared Technical space remains.” (Technical Corridors)
reviews.expected_answer: Remove miniature, discard injuries, return matching token to bag; keep Noise. Characters barred except Mechanic Technical Corridors card and Technical Corridor Plans Item; Doors never placed there.
reviews.reason: All miniature/injury/token/Noise outcomes, Character exceptions and no Technical Doors are explicit.

reviews.question: Describe an ordinary Shoot versus Melee Action: card/ammo costs, target location, Contamination, a miss, and the two-hit die result.

requested_parts.part: Shoot one Action card and one Ammo; same-Room target
Melee one Action card and Contamination to Action discard before target
Melee miss inflicts one Serious Wound
Shoot miss causes no wound penalty
requested_parts.reason: No Shoot-miss result is stated in this answer.

requested_parts.part: Shoot double-hit two Injuries versus Melee one

reviews.observed_answer:
1. Cost 1 Action card plus 1 Ammo; choose Weapon and one Intruder in same Room, discard Ammo, roll combat die.
2. Cost 1 Action card; draw Contamination onto Action discard pile, target Intruder in same Room and roll; any miss causes shooter 1 Serious Wound.
3. Shoot double-hit inflicts 2 Injuries before weapon modifiers; Melee treats double-hit as 1 Injury.
4. Melee draw is not a cost card and cannot pay Actions.
reviews.observed_evidence: “Cost 1 Action card plus 1 Ammo; choose Weapon and one Intruder in same Room, discard Ammo, roll combat die.” (Combat)

The question asks ordinary Shoot versus Melee including a miss, but the answer never states that Shoot misses have no wound penalty. Calling the Melee attacker shooter in clause 2 is treated as a terminology slip within the clearly Melee procedure, not an affirmative Shoot ruling. The missing Shoot miss result makes this partial.

reviews.question: After damage, how are Larva, Adult and Queen death checked, when is a Carcass placed, and what if a Queen check draws a Retreat arrow?

requested_parts.required: Draw 1 Intruder Attack card; blood <= current total Injuries means death.
Draw 2 Intruder Attack cards, sum blood, and use the same <= current total Injuries death comparison. Accept a comparison established within this answer and a clear parallel Queen adaptation.
A dead Adult leaves a Carcass in its Room; a general non-Larva death rule suffices.
A dead Queen leaves a Carcass in its Room; a general non-Larva death rule suffices.
A dead Larva leaves no Carcass.
An arrow on either Queen card causes retreat in place of numerical death resolution. Accept an unconditional Queen-flees outcome following the normal numerical check. No reservation about precedence.

reviews.observed_answer:
1. At 1 Injury Larva dies; remove miniature and no Carcass.
2. Draw 1 Intruder Attack card for Injury Effect, compare blood to total current Injuries; blood ≤ injuries kills Adult, otherwise survives.
3. Draw 2 Attack cards and sum blood; sum ≤ current Injuries kills Queen, otherwise survives.
4. Adult/Queen death removes miniature and places Carcass in Room; any Retreat arrow in Queen’s two-card check triggers retreat instead of numeric result (Queen retreats if either arrow).
5. After Queen damage check, draw 2 Attack cards and sum blood; if either shows Retreat arrow, retreat instead: draw Event card, move via Corridor number in its Intruder movement section, then discard Event card.
reviews.observed_evidence: “At 1 Injury Larva dies; remove miniature and no Carcass.” (Intruder Injuries and death; Intruder Retreat); After Queen damage check, draw 2 Attack cards and sum blood; if either shows Retreat arrow, retreat instead: draw Event card, move via Corridor number in its Intruder movement section, then discard Event card.
reviews.expected_answer: Larva dies at 1 injury without Carcass. Adult draws one Attack card blood, dies if blood <= current injuries and leaves Carcass. Queen draws two, sums blood and compares same way; any Retreat arrow causes retreat via Event-card corridor number, discard Event, rather than normal numerical resolution.
reviews.reason: All seven adjudicated parts are explicit: Larva one-Injury death/no Carcass; Adult one-card <= check; Queen two-card sum <= check; Adult/Queen Carcasses; either Queen arrow substitutes retreat. The fifth clause is a repeated description of the Queen check, not an explicit instruction to perform an extra check. Event routing/discard are unasked but accurate.

reviews.question: A Character Escapes a Room with two Intruders toward an empty unexplored Room. When do attacks occur, who is targeted, what happens if they die, and what follows if they survive?
reviews.observed_answer:
1. Before Escape move, resolve one Intruder Attack per Intruder, largest first: Queen, Breeder, Adult, Larva.
2. Escape attacks target the escaping Character.
3. If Character dies, their Corpse remains in origin Room and movement does not complete.
4. If survives, move to chosen neighboring explored or unexplored Room; resolve exploration if needed and Noise roll if destination empty.
reviews.observed_evidence: “Before Escape move, resolve one Intruder Attack per Intruder, largest first: Queen, Breeder, Adult, Larva.” (Character Escape)
reviews.expected_answer: Pay Movement cost 1, choose neighboring Room. Before moving resolve separate Attack from each Intruder targeting escaper. Death leaves Corpse in starting Room; survival completes move and standard exploration/Noise.
reviews.reason: Explicit separate pre-move attacks target the escaper, death leaves Corpse in origin and survival completes ordinary neighboring-room exploration/Noise. Movement cost is unasked context here.

reviews.question: In an ordinary Intruder Attack with several Characters, how is the target chosen and ties broken; how is a hit determined; what changes for Larva and where does its Contamination go?
reviews.observed_answer:
1. Among Characters present, target one with fewest Action cards; tie goes to First Player token holder or next in turn order. Surprise Attack instead targets Encounter-triggering Character.
2. For non-Larva draw Attack card: matching Intruder type symbol means resolve card effect; otherwise miss; ignore blood icon and discard card.
3. Draw no Attack card; remove Larva from board and put on target Character board, give target 1 Contamination.
4. Attacking Larva disappears, existing stays, Character gets Contamination but is not automatically killed.
5. Contamination goes atop target’s Action discard pile.
reviews.observed_evidence: “Among Characters present, target one with fewest Action cards; tie goes to First Player token holder or next in turn order. Surprise Attack instead targets Encounter-triggering Character.” (Intruder Attack; Infest)
reviews.expected_answer: Fewest Action cards in hand; tie First Player or next in turn order. Matching attacker symbol on drawn Attack card means resolve effect; otherwise miss; ignore blood and discard card. Larva draws no Attack card: place miniature on target Character board and give Contamination on top of Action discard.
reviews.reason: Target/tie selection, matching-symbol test, discard/ignore-blood, Larva no-card placement and Contamination destination are explicit; duplicate-Larva context is accurate.

reviews.question: At three Serious Wounds, does dressing one prevent death from a Light Wound? What happens at a third Light Wound otherwise, what does Heal remove, and where do a dead Characters Corpse and Heavy Objects go?
reviews.observed_answer:
1. Dressing only suppresses Serious Wound card effect; it still counts, so at 3 Serious Wounds any further Wound kills.
2. Clear Light Wound track and suffer 1 Serious Wound.
3. Remove a Light Wound or discard a Dressed Serious Wound as the healing effect specifies.
4. Place Character Corpse Object in death Room and drop all Heavy Objects there.
reviews.observed_evidence: “Dressing only suppresses Serious Wound card effect; it still counts, so at 3 Serious Wounds any further Wound kills.” (Character Wounds and death)
reviews.expected_answer: No: dressed still counts; any further Wound kills at three Serious. Third Light clears Light track and causes Serious Wound. Heal removes specified Light Wound or discards dressed Serious card. Place Corpse and drop Heavy Objects in death Room.
reviews.reason: Dressed wounds retain count; fatal threshold, third-Light conversion, Heal and death-room Corpse/Heavy Objects all match.

reviews.question: Contrast Canteen/Shower scanning with Surgery: which cards are scanned and removed, how is a Larva handled, and what costs or turn consequences follow Surgery?
reviews.observed_answer:
1. Scan all Contamination cards in hand only; remove non-Infected cards. Infected stays; if no Larva before scan place Larva, if already Larva die and place Creeper in Room.
2. Scan all Contamination cards in deck, hand and discard; remove all Infected cards and remove Larva if present.
3. Then suffer 1 Light Wound, automatically pass, shuffle all cards including entire hand and remaining Contamination into Action deck; hand empty until next turn.
reviews.observed_evidence: “Scan all Contamination cards in hand only; remove non-Infected cards. Infected stays; if no Larva before scan place Larva, if already Larva die and place Creeper in Room.” (Contamination; Canteen/Shower; Surgery)
reviews.expected_answer: Canteen/Shower optionally scan hand Contamination, remove non-Infected; infected gives Larva and retains card, existing Larva means death/Creeper. Canteen heals 1 Light; Shower removes Slime. Surgery scans deck/hand/discard, removes infected and Larva, then 1 Light Wound, automatic pass, shuffle all cards including hand into deck; empty hand until next turn.
reviews.reason: Correct hand-only ordinary scan/removal and preexisting-Larva outcomes contrasted with all-zone Surgery removal, Light Wound, pass and entire-hand reshuffle. Canteen healing and Shower Slime removal are outside the asked scanning comparison.

reviews.question: How can uncarried Eggs be destroyed with Shoot/Melee, grenades, Molotov and Fire; which Melee penalties are waived, when is Noise rolled and when is the Nest destroyed?

requested_parts.part: Shoot/Melee each Injury destroys one uncarried Egg
Successful Egg Melee retains ordinary Contamination; miss waives Contamination and Wound
Grenade two, Molotov one, Fire one per step
Nest destroyed when no board Eggs remain

reviews.observed_answer:
1. In Room with uncarried Eggs, each Injury destroys one Egg; successful Egg Melee keeps normal Contamination draw, missed Egg Melee causes neither Contamination nor Wound.
2. Grenade destroys 2 Eggs; Molotov destroys 1; Fire destroys 1 uncarried Egg per Fire Damage step (2 with Vulnerability to Fire).
3. After every single Egg-destruction attempt roll Noise; when no Eggs remain on Intruder board, Nest is destroyed.
4. Summary says manuals do not resolve how missed Egg Melee waiver reconciles with normal pre-roll Contamination draw; no refund or alternate draw timing is specified.
reviews.observed_evidence: “In Room with uncarried Eggs, each Injury destroys one Egg; successful Egg Melee keeps normal Contamination draw, missed Egg Melee causes neither Contamination nor Wound.” (Eggs and the Nest)
reviews.expected_answer: Each Injury from Shoot/Melee destroys 1 uncarried Egg. Successful Egg Melee retains the ordinary draw of 1 Contamination card onto the Action discard pile. On a missed Egg Melee, no Contamination card and no Wound are suffered. The sources do not specify how the normal pre-roll draw and miss waiver are reconciled; no refund or delayed draw is invented. Grenade destroys 2 Eggs, Molotov 1; Noise after every destruction attempt including miss. Fire destroys 1 uncarried Egg each Fire Damage step. Nest destroyed once all its Eggs taken/destroyed; mark Injury in Nest.
reviews.reason: Every asked Egg weapon count, successful-Melee Contamination, missed-Melee waiver, Noise-after-every-attempt and no-Eggs Nest-destruction condition is supplied. The unasked missed-draw execution caveat is truthful and causes no factual or strict deduction; the reader's support label is not a grade.

reviews.question: What permits or prevents entering an Escape Pod, what must you resolve first, how many Characters and Heavy Objects fit, and what are the options and consequences when you wait?
reviews.observed_answer:
1. Pay 2 Action cards for Evacuation Section Room Action; Pod must be unlocked and have free character slot; no entry if Intruder or Malfunction in Section. Roll Noise first; Intruder present or appearing makes attempt fail.
2. Pod holds 2 Characters; Heavy Objects use no Character space. After boarding, may launch immediately: remove Pod and occupants from play; they count as arriving on Earth but still face final Contamination and Objective checks.
3. Wait passes current turn and counts as present in Section for bag-development Noise rolls. At start of first round in each later Player Phase choose exactly one: keep waiting/pass, launch, or exit free to Section Room and take full 2-Action round.
4. Second Character boarding may launch both immediately. Intruder appearing in Section returns all Pod occupants to Section Room. Malfunction while waiting still permits wait/launch/exit, but prevents new entry.
reviews.observed_evidence: “Pay 2 Action cards for Evacuation Section Room Action; Pod must be unlocked and have free character slot; no entry if Intruder or Malfunction in Section. Roll Noise first; Intruder present or appearing makes attempt fail.” (Escape Pods)
reviews.expected_answer: Use corresponding Evacuation Room Action cost 2, unlocked Pod with free space, no Intruder/Malfunction. Roll Noise first and fail if Intruder reaches Room. Two Character spaces; Heavy Objects use none. Enter then launch immediately or wait and pass current turn. At start of first round next Player Phase choose wait/pass, launch, or free exit followed by a full two-Action round. Intruder appearing in Section returns all Pod occupants; another boarder may immediately launch.
reviews.reason: All entry and pre-entry Noise conditions, two-Character/no-Object-space capacity, immediate launch, waiting/pass/Noise, later first-round options, second-boarder launch and Intruder/Malfunction consequences are explicit.

reviews.question: Give the endgame checks in order. What happens with two Damaged Engines, a non-Earth destination (including Quarantine/Mars), and an infected survivor or one carrying a Larva? Do pod passengers need Contamination checks?
reviews.observed_answer:
1. If at least one survivor, check Engines, Coordinates, Contamination, Objectives in that order.
2. Two or three Damaged Engines cause ship explosion and everyone aboard, including sleepers, dies; launched Pod passengers are away.
3. Non-Earth destination kills hibernating Characters; ship remains undestroyed and Intruders live. Quarantine Objective sleeper survives if destination Mars.
4. Every survivor including Pod passengers is checked: without Larva, scan all Contamination in deck/hand/discard; if none Infected, stop with no four-card draw. If any Infected or Larva present, shuffle all Action/Contamination cards from zones and draw 4; any Contamination among four kills, otherwise survive.
5. Living characters reveal Objective; survival alone is insufficient.
reviews.observed_evidence: “If at least one survivor, check Engines, Coordinates, Contamination, Objectives in that order.” (Victory Check)
reviews.expected_answer: Engines then Coordinates then Contamination then Objectives. If ship survives to checks: two/three Damaged explodes kills all aboard incl Intruders; non-Earth kills sleepers but ship/Intruders survive, Quarantine sleeper survives Mars. All survivors including launched pod passengers scan all Contamination; any infected triggers shuffle all Action/Contamination draw 4, any Contamination kills else survives. Larva skips scanning and directly does shuffle/draw. Survivors then reveal/check chosen Objective.
reviews.reason: Correct order, damaged-Engine destruction, destination/Quarantine outcomes and all-survivor scan versus Larva/infected shuffle/draw-four branches; Pod and Objective checks explicit.

reviews.question: How are the basic and additional Room tiles and Exploration tokens placed at setup; what Coordinates, Destination, Time, Engines, Eggs and Weaknesses start on the board?
reviews.observed_answer:

Random face-down Coordinates, Destination B, Time green. Each numbered Engine has shuffled Damaged/Working pair face down, top true status. Five Eggs, three random face-down Weaknesses.

reviews.question: How are Player Numbers assigned and Characters drafted; what does each Character receive and where do Characters and the initial Corpse begin? Are Quest Items usable immediately?
reviews.observed_answer:
1. Deal numbered Help cards 1 through player count randomly; number also on Inventory sets order and matters to some Objectives.
2. Deal each Corporate and Personal Objective before Character draft; Player 1 draws 2 Character draft cards, reveals both, keeps one and shuffles other back, then others in number order.

1. Cannot Interrupt remote Captain Order via Intercom if you are not in same Room as Character performing interrupted Action.
2. Passing does not bar Interruption; FAQ permits it after pass, subject to same-Room requirement.

reviews.expected_answer: No remote Interruption: must share Room with Character performing Action. Passing does not bar playing Interruption.
reviews.reason: Same-Room requirement forbids the remote Interruption, while passing does not bar it.

reviews.question: Describe Antidote: scan scope, removed cards, new Contamination, reshuffling, hand retention and passing; how does Surgery differ?
reviews.observed_answer:
1. Scan all own Contamination in hand, deck and discard; remove all Infected cards from game.
2. Gain 1 new Contamination, then reshuffle it with non-Infected scanned Contamination and Action cards, except cards retained in hand.
3. Then pass; may keep hand cards.
4. Surgery scans same zones and removes infected cards, removes Larva if present, gives no new Contamination, suffers 1 Light Wound, then automatically passes and shuffles entire hand plus remaining cards into Action deck (empty hand).
reviews.observed_evidence: “Scan all own Contamination in hand, deck and discard; remove all Infected cards from game.” (FAQ: Antidote; Surgery)
reviews.expected_answer: Scan all Contamination from hand/deck/discard, remove all Infected from game, take one new Contamination, reshuffle it with all non-Infected scanned Contamination and Action cards except cards left in hand, then pass. May retain hand cards. Surgery instead shuffles entire hand too and does not gain extra Contamination (and its own wound/removal procedure still applies).
reviews.reason: All Antidote scan/removal/new-card/reshuffle/retained-hand/pass parts and Surgery contrasts including Larva, wound, no new card and full-hand shuffle explicit.

reviews.question: An unslimed Character first enters the unexplored Room Covered With Slime by ordinary Movement and reveals a Silence Exploration token. Resolve Slime and the token in order, including the resulting Intruder/Noise effects, whether a separate normal Noise roll is made, and where the Exploration token goes.

requested_parts.part: Gain Slime on entry before resolving Exploration
Move all eligible neighboring non-Combat Intruders
If none eligible, connected unmarked Noise including Technical

reviews.observed_answer:
1. On ordinary Movement into Slime Room, first gain Slime, then reveal/resolve Exploration Silence; because now slimed, Silence becomes Danger.
2. Move all neighboring Intruders not in Combat into this Room; if none eligible, place Noise in every connected unmarked Corridor, including Technical if entrance.
3. No separate normal Noise roll because Exploration token resolves Silence/Danger instead. After resolution remove Exploration token from game into box.
reviews.observed_evidence: “On ordinary Movement into Slime Room, first gain Slime, then reveal/resolve Exploration Silence; because now slimed, Silence becomes Danger.” (Room Covered With Slime; Exploration tokens; Noise roll)
reviews.expected_answer: Gain Slime immediately on entering the Room, before resolving its Exploration token. Because the Character is now Slimed, the Silence Exploration effect becomes Danger. Move ALL eligible neighboring Intruders not in Combat into the Room; if there are none (or all are in Combat), place Noise in every connected Corridor lacking Noise, including the Technical Corridors space if connected. Do not make a separate normal Noise roll for this Movement. After resolving it, remove the Exploration token from the game to the box.
reviews.reason: Correct first Slime then Silence-to-Danger, all eligible non-Combat neighbors or connected unmarked Noise including Technical, no separate normal roll and removal of resolved token to box.
